questions.now: The rule quoted from our handbook, with the section shown.

result.query: duplicate charge refund approve without escalation

results.heading: Duplicate charges
results.text:
## Duplicate charges
A duplicate charge is refunded in full within 5 business days once Billing confirms it. Agents on Tier 1 may approve duplicate-charge refunds up to $600 without escalation. Billing confirms and approves duplicate charges over $600.

results.heading: Escalation runbook
results.text:
# Escalation runbook

This is Harbor Cloud's own runbook. The triggers below are our rules.

results.heading: When to escalate
results.text:
## When to escalate
Hand a ticket to Tier 2 when it is a confirmed bug, involves data loss, or has missed its first-response target. Urgent tickets go straight to Tier 2. Escalate to the Escalations team for any urgent ticket older than 4 hours without a resolution or any ticket from an Enterprise customer with CSAT below 3.

questions.ask: When am I supposed to escalate an urgent ticket?
questions.reply: Two triggers from our runbook: any urgent ticket older than 4 hours without a resolution, or any ticket from an Enterprise customer with CSAT below 3. Set it to escalated, assign an Escalations agent, and don't promise the customer a timeline until that agent has triaged it.
questions.before: Ask a senior colleague, or search the runbook.
questions.now: The two triggers and the steps, quoted from our runbook.

result.query: escalate urgent ticket hours escalations team

results.heading: When to escalate
results.text:
## When to escalate
Hand a ticket to Tier 2 when it is a confirmed bug, involves data loss, or has missed its first-response target. Urgent tickets go straight to Tier 2. Escalate to the Escalations team for any urgent ticket older than 4 hours without a resolution or any ticket from an Enterprise customer with CSAT below 3.

results.heading: How to escalate
results.text:
## How to escalate
Set status to escalated, assign to an Escalations agent, and post the ticket link in the escalations channel with the customer's plan and the time the target was missed. Do not promise the customer a timeline before the Escalations agent has triaged the ticket.

results.heading: Warning signs
results.text:
## Warning signs
An account shows a warning sign when it has an overdue invoice, an open urgent ticket, or an average CSAT below 3. A warning sign comes up on the call before any talk of renewal terms.

questions.ask: What's the first-response target for a High ticket from a Business-plan customer?
questions.reply: Four business hours for High, and Business-plan customers also get a named escalation contact. The 30-minute target in that section is for urgent tickets only. Both sections are in the panel with the matching lines highlighted.
questions.before: The service levels document was opened and read through.
questions.now: The target and the named-contact rule, quoted from our service levels.

result.query: first response target high business hours plan

results.heading: First response targets
results.text:
## First response targets
- Urgent: 1 hour, 24x7
- High: 4 business hours
- Normal: 1 business day
- Low: 2 business days

Urgent tickets are answered and worked around the clock. Everything else is answered and worked in business hours.

results.heading: Business and Enterprise plans
results.text:
## Business and Enterprise plans
Business and Enterprise customers get a named escalation contact and a 30-minute urgent first-response target during business hours.

results.heading: When to escalate
results.text:
## When to escalate
Hand a ticket to Tier 2 when it is a confirmed bug, involves data loss, or has missed its first-response target. Urgent tickets go straight to Tier 2. Escalate to the Escalations team for any urgent ticket older than 4 hours without a resolution or any ticket from an Enterprise customer with CSAT below 3.
